summary: 64-year-old hypertensive man with sudden tearing epigastric pain radiating between the shoulder blades; BP 188/104 right arm vs 152/90 left; amylase normal. Must not be labelled pancreatitis or ulcer: CT angiography; no antiplatelets/anticoagulation.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Sudden severe upper abdominal and back pain
inputs.hpi: Sudden severe tearing pain in the upper abdomen going through to between the shoulder blades one hour ago, maximal at onset. Poorly controlled blood pressure. Felt faint. No vomiting, no alcohol excess.

exam.general: Distressed, sweaty. Pulse 96/min. BP 188/104 right arm, 152/90 left arm (pulse and BP differential).
exam.cardiovascular: Early diastolic murmur at the left sternal edge.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding, no pulsatile mass.

imaging.name: ECG
imaging.result: Sinus rhythm, left ventricular hypertrophy, no acute ST changes.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute aortic dissection
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Sudden tearing epigastric/interscapular pain with inter-arm BP difference and aortic regurgitation murmur — acute aortic dissection until CT angiography excludes it.

mustNotMiss.note: An abdominal aortic aneurysm entry does not count: the work-up and the harm (antithrombotics) differ.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: pancreatitis, inguinal hernia, cholecystitis (epigastric pain + radiation to back = pancreatitis pattern); no dissection node. Symptom inference ranks ruptured AAA #1 and does not list dissection in the top 5.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add a dissection rule/prompt: abrupt/tearing pain to back + BP/pulse differential or hypertension → "Acute aortic syndrome: CT angiography; avoid antithrombotics" (ESC 2014).

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Symptom inference has an "Aortic dissection" entry but it needs chest-pain chips ("Tearing / ripping"); with abdominal chips it is outside the top 5.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No protocol (I71.0) and no prompt suggests CT angiography.

mustExclude.note: Antiplatelet, anticoagulant or thrombolytic treatment in aortic dissection can be fatal.

guideline.name: 2014 ESC Guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of aortic diseases
guideline.section: Acute aortic syndrome: high-risk features (abrupt tearing pain, pulse/BP differential, aortic regurgitation murmur); CT angiography first-line when stable; heart-rate and blood-pressure control (IV beta-blocker); urgent cardiothoracic/vascular referral
guideline.citation: Erbel R, Aboyans V, Boileau C, et al. Eur Heart J. 2014;35:2873–2926.

rationale: Dangerous mimic of an upper GI emergency: epigastric pain to the back suggests pancreatitis or a posterior ulcer, but a normal amylase, abrupt tearing onset, an inter-arm BP difference and an AR murmur point to dissection. The harmful path is an ACS or GI plan with antithrombotics.

authoring.author: Claude (upper-GI cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations written from the guideline texts, not yet checked against the source (verified: false).
